claim: The most relevant source reports a dataset slicing protocol running from N=100 to N=15,000 rows.
quote: this study employed a large-scale dataset slicing protocol (from N=100 to N=15,000 rows) alongside a matched-volume quality ablation.

claim: It finds that models are indistinguishable at small scales.
quote: These results reveal a Small-Sample Illusion: models perform indistinguishably at small scales.

claim: It adds that a gradient-boosted tree advantage emerges as sample sizes grow.
quote: As sample sizes increase, a distinct gradient-boosted tree advantage emerges.

claim: A large benchmark that accounts for hyperparameter search reports that tree-based models remain state-of-the-art on medium-sized data (about 10K samples), even without accounting for their superior speed.
quote: Results show that tree-based models remain state-of-the-art on medium-sized data ($\sim$10K samples) even without accounting for their superior speed.

claim: The same work notes that the gap stays wide across random-search budgets.
quote: We observed that tree-based models are superior for every random search budget, and the performance gap stays wide even after a large number of random search iteration.

claim: It also cautions that this might change with added regularization.
quote: However, this might no longer be true when adding additional regularization techniques to our random search, such as data augmentation.

claim: It also reports that this advantage grows with tuning time.
quote: As more time is invested, the performance gap with XGBoost increases, and the results get even more significant

claim: A later TabPFN version is described as a tabular foundation model that outperforms all previous methods on datasets with up to 10,000 samples by a wide margin.
quote: a tabular foundation model that outperforms all previous methods on datasets with up to 10,000 samples by a wide margin

claim: Statements that deep learning trails GBDTs on small data are reported secondhand. TabPFN's authors note that earlier work found deep learning baselines do not outperform or match GBDTs for small to medium-sized data.
quote: We note that previous works have found that DL baselines do not outperform or match the performance of GBDT or AutoML methods for small to medium-sized tabular data (< 10,000 samples; while matching GBDT performance on larger datasets)
locator: sec. EVALUATION ON TABULAR ML TASKS, para 48

claim: HyperTab, a small-data neural method, states that it is especially challenging to surpass tree-like ensembles such as XGBoost or Random Forests on small datasets (under 1k samples).
quote: It is especially challenging to surpass the performance of tree-like ensembles, such as XGBoost or Random Forests, on small-sized datasets (less than 1k samples).
